source_name: CBCG — Instant plaćanja (TIPS Clone)
why_relevant: Names the technology/operating model for Montenegro's national instant payment scheme: a TIPS Clone supplied by Banca d'Italia on behalf of the Eurosystem, with ECB and World Bank involvement, live 20 July 2026 with all 11 banks participating simultaneously. This is the single highest-leverage country-wide vendor signal in the cell: it fixes the core settlement platform and creates a pipeline of bank-side adaptation work (ISO 20022, channel, fraud, core integration) for third-party vendors.

source_name: CBCG — Pravila platnog sistema CBCG (payment system rules PDF)
why_relevant: The binding operating rules of the national payment system: participation criteria (personnel, organisational, technical), connectivity/technical requirements, message standards and settlement windows. Technical annexes of such rules are where interface specs, certification obligations and implicitly the platform's technology are revealed.

source_name: CBCG — RTGS sistem participant/agent registry PDF
why_relevant: Structured register entry for the RTGS system itself (operator, legal basis, participants). Machine-friendly, low-volume, high-signal artefact for tracking who is connected to national settlement.

source_name: CBCG — Saopštenja / Aktuelno (press releases)
why_relevant: Where CBCG announces infrastructure milestones with named counterparties: SEPA membership, SEPA scheme application, first SEPA transactions, TIPS Clone letters of intent and go-live. These releases are the primary dated record of country-level infrastructure and partner events.

source_name: nabavke.com — Montenegrin public procurement aggregator (CBCG buyer profile)
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator of Montenegrin tenders that indexes CBCG notices and outcome documents (e.g. 'Obavještenje o ishodu postupka'). Useful as a search/archive layer over procurement when the CBCG board itself only shows current notices.

source_name: Banca d'Italia — TIPS Clone / Western Balkans news and TIPS service pages
why_relevant: Banca d'Italia is the technology provider/operator of the TIPS Clone platform used by Montenegro. Its newsroom carries the letters of intent, country accessions and go-live announcements for the whole Western Balkans programme — a supra-national vendor signal that covers ME, AL, BA, XK and (optionally) MK at once.

source_name: ECB — MIP news / TARGET services (Western Balkans instant settlement roll-out)
why_relevant: The ECB Governing Council approved the TIPS Clone arrangement and publishes MIP (Market Infrastructure and Payments) news covering roll-out, scope and governance. Authoritative confirmation layer above CBCG and Banca d'Italia, and the source of TIPS technical documentation that vendors must build against.

source_name: European Payments Council — Register of Participants (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD, SRTP, SPAA, OCT Inst, VOP)
why_relevant: Definitive, scheme-by-scheme list of which Montenegrin PSPs have adhered to which SEPA scheme, with BICs and adherence dates. Adherence timing is a direct readout of each bank's technical readiness project — and therefore of vendor engagements. Downloadable structured data.

source_name: EPC — Adherence Guide and List of SEPA Scheme Countries (documents)
why_relevant: Records Montenegro's admission to SEPA geographical scope and the operational readiness date — the hard dates that gate bank-side implementation programmes. The Adherence Guide defines the NASO role that shapes who coordinates the national migration.

source_name: Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (UBCG) — SEPA hub and news
why_relevant: The Montenegrin banking association coordinates the national SEPA effort (NASO-type function) across all 11 member banks. Its SEPA section and news stream are the industry-side counterpart to CBCG announcements and typically surface working groups, timelines and the consultants/vendors supporting migration.

source_name: Mastercard Europe Newsroom — press releases and news briefs
why_relevant: Scheme-side channel where Mastercard announces bank, fintech and processor partnerships across Europe including CEE/SEE. Montenegro-specific items are rare, so this is a low-yield/high-value monitor: when a ME item appears it usually names the issuing bank and the enabling technology partner.

source_name: Visa Partner Directory (Visa Ready certified partners)
why_relevant: Searchable directory of Visa-certified technology partners by capability and market. Certification status is a proxy for who is technically able to serve ME issuers/acquirers, and the directory itself is a pointer to vendor entities to profile.

source_name: World Bank — Montenegro FSAP Technical Note (payments and settlements infrastructure)
why_relevant: Independent assessment describing the actual architecture: CBCG-owned RTGS+DNS as the only interbank infrastructure, the Central Depository Agency as CSD, and an interoperable ATM/POS network whose routing and settlement runs over the international card scheme networks (i.e. no domestic card switch). This is the best single authoritative statement of the ME infrastructure baseline, and the World Bank is also a named supporter of the TIPS Clone project.

source_name: EEAS / EU Delegation to Montenegro — payments integration statements
why_relevant: The EU delegation co-announces SEPA milestones for Montenegro, tying them to accession conditionality. Useful for forward-looking timing signals on further infrastructure alignment (ISO 20022, instant payments regulation, TARGET access) that drive vendor demand.

source_name: CBCG — Centralni registar transakcionih računa & e-services / PKI pages
why_relevant: Adjacent CBCG-operated infrastructure: the central register of transaction accounts and the CBCG's own PKI issuing certificates for the closed payment-system environment. Both are separately procured systems and therefore separate vendor footprints inside the same operator.

source_name: Montenegrobusiness / monte.business — English-language ME payments coverage
why_relevant: English-language secondary coverage of ME payment infrastructure events (TIPS Clone signing, instant payments readiness). Lower authority but useful for quickly surfacing events to non-Montenegrin-reading analysts and for cross-checking dates.

source_name: CBCG — Bankarski sistem (banking system section)
why_relevant: English-language parent of the bank register; useful for stable English entity naming and for locating supervisory reporting attached to the same section. Confirms CBCG runs parallel /me/ and /eng/ trees.

source_name: CBCG — Pružaoci finansijskih usluga (non-bank financial service providers)
why_relevant: Index of CBCG-supervised non-bank providers: leasing companies, factoring, purchase-of-receivables firms, microcredit financial institutions and credit guarantee funds. Expands the licensed-actor map beyond banks/PIs into adjacent lending and BNPL-like players.

source_name: CBCG — Mikrokreditne finansijske institucije (MFI list)
why_relevant: Named list of licensed microcredit financial institutions — a distinct buyer segment for lending/collections/digital onboarding technology, absent from bank and PI registers. Note both spellings appear in CBCG URLs ('institucije' and a misspelled 'insitucije' variant), so both paths should be crawled.

source_name: CBCG — Usluge kreditnog registra (Credit Register services)
why_relevant: Describes the CBCG credit register and who its reporting participants are — i.e. the set of institutions legally obliged to report credit data, which is another way to enumerate licensed lenders and to understand a shared national data-infrastructure procurement area.

source_name: CBCG — Finansijski sistem Crne Gore (financial system overview)
why_relevant: Gives the official taxonomy and headcount of institution types in the ME financial system, which is the sanity check that the register crawl has full coverage (no institution class missed).

source_name: CRPS / eFirma portal (crps.me)
why_relevant: The registration-side portal of CRPS: filings, forms, notices, downloads and the entry point to the beneficial-ownership register. Its news/notices pages announce register changes (e-registration since Dec 2020, RSV since Aug 2021) that affect collection method.

source_name: CRPS — Registar stvarnih vlasnika (beneficial ownership register)
why_relevant: Beneficial-ownership register established at CRPS on 1 Aug 2021 under the AML/CFT law. Critical for resolving who actually controls ME payment institutions, e-money issuers and IT vendors — often foreign parents that connect ME actors to regional group strategies.

source_name: IRMS Portal (Uprava prihoda i carina) — Pretraga registra privrednih subjekata
why_relevant: Newer Tax/Revenue Administration portal exposing a public business-entity register search — a likely successor or parallel front-end to pretraga.crps.me. Worth tracking because a migration here would change the canonical collection endpoint for all company-resolution work.

source_name: MONSTAT — Statistički biznis registar (SBR) methodology and releases
why_relevant: The Statistical Business Register defines the population of active business entities in ME, classified by KD 2010 (= NACE Rev.2). The methodology document explains how activity codes and activity/size/municipality breakdowns are derived — needed to interpret any 'how many IT/financial firms exist in ME' number correctly.

source_name: MONSTAT — 'Broj i struktura poslovnih subjekata' annual releases (saopštenja)
why_relevant: Annual statistical releases giving counts and structure of active business entities by NACE sector, size and municipality. Quantifies the addressable population of financial-sector and IT/J-sector firms in ME, and the year-on-year series shows sector growth or contraction.

source_name: Data.gov.me — national open data portal (datasets)
why_relevant: Government open-data portal that may publish machine-readable versions of registers and administrative datasets (including 'uprava' group datasets). If any CRPS/CBCG/MONSTAT list is mirrored here in CSV/JSON, it is a far cheaper and more legally comfortable collection route than scraping.
